Source: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0, https://github.com/GPUOpen-Effects/FidelityFX-FSR, release tag `v1.0.2` (commit `a21ffb8`): `ffx-fsr/ffx_a.h` and `ffx-fsr/ffx_fsr1.h`, unmodified. License in LICENSE (MIT; the repository's `license.txt`).
sha256: `ffx_a.h` f60e2722fcd13989523b9164d776ab382b3692791767f3bf8bb19967f763f3fb, `ffx_fsr1.h` 93c3922362ea7fc99cbcc698ca30c98de4f8c246d1fbb0b09e015ddef38ce3a5, `LICENSE` db089274ce766da70f5b7d791029c3486f9f9e27c8c79c652689603d3192e802.
Use: the Vulkan backend's window presenter (Windows, Linux) runs FSR 1's two passes, EASU (edge-adaptive spatial upsampling) then RCAS (robust contrast-adaptive sharpening), when `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=fsr` and the picture is shown larger than the game renders it (`dm/gfx/hostvk/vk_present.c`). The GLSL compute wrappers `dm/gfx/hostvk/shaders/fsr_easu.comp` and `fsr_rcas.comp` include these headers with the 32-bit path (`A_GPU`, `A_GLSL`, `FSR_EASU_F`, `FSR_RCAS_F`) and define the fetch callbacks; `dm/gfx/hostvk/shaders/gen_spirv.sh` compiles them into the committed SPIR-V headers, so building needs neither glslang nor these files. Apple builds never compile them.
